questions.subject: bss

Uma previsão do tempo para amanhã

questions.hint: Fontes são vestígios deixados pelas pessoas do passado.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Num mapa com escala 1:100.000, a distância entre duas cidades é de 5 cm. Qual é a distância real, em quilômetros?

questions.q: Por que os rios foram tão importantes para as primeiras civilizações, como a egípcia e a mesopotâmica?

en.topic: Term 1 review: sentences, punctuation and narrative writing

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is a simple sentence?
options: The dog barked, and the cat ran.
When the dog barked, the cat ran.
The dog barked because it was hungry.
questions.hint: A simple sentence has one main clause.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is a compound sentence?
options: I was tired, but I finished my homework.
Although I was tired, I finished my homework.
questions.answer: I was tired, but I finished my homework.
questions.hint: Look for two main clauses joined by and, but or so.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is a complex sentence?
options: Although it was raining, we went outside.
It was raining, so we stayed in.
questions.answer: Although it was raining, we went outside.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word is a subordinating conjunction?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses an apostrophe correctly for one girl?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which phrase correctly shows a meeting belonging to many teachers?
questions.hint: For plural nouns ending in s, where does the apostrophe go?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence contains a comma splice?
options: It was late, we went home.
It was late, so we went home.
It was late; we went home.
Because it was late, we went home.
questions.answer: It was late, we went home.
questions.hint: A comma splice joins two main clauses with only a comma.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
options: The sun set; the sky turned orange.
The sun; set the sky turned orange.
The sun set the; sky turned orange.
The; sun set the sky turned orange.
questions.answer: The sun set; the sky turned orange.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which line of direct speech is punctuated correctly?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is an imperative sentence?
questions.hint: Imperatives give commands or instructions.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which punctuation mark usually ends an exclamatory sentence?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word should be corrected in this sentence: "Their going to the park after lunch."
questions.hint: Should it be 'they are'?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: A story told using 'I' and 'me' by one of the characters is written in the:

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence 'shows' fear rather than 'telling' it?
options: Her hands trembled as she reached for the handle.
She was frightened of the door.
questions.answer: Her hands trembled as she reached for the handle.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is the most engaging opening line for a mystery story?
options: The box had not been there yesterday.
This is a story about a box.
I am going to tell you about a box.
questions.answer: The box had not been there yesterday.
questions.hint: Which one makes the reader ask a question?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Rewrite the sentence "The house was scary." so that it shows, rather than tells, that the house was scary.
questions.hint: Use details the reader could see or hear.

questions.subject: en_read

questions.q: Read: "Ella stared at the empty seat next to her and pushed her lunch away." How might Ella be feeling? Use evidence from the sentence.
